architecture: v7 (re-root after the repair's judge SEND_BACK on architecture 6: an awarding body's 2027 pass mark on its heat pump installer theory paper after a test-vendor change, the old standard carried across through the candidates who sat both papers, their second attempts read against the retest gain measured on candidates who sat the old paper twice)
slot_note: re-root of task474 in the same objective (Data Extraction & Conformation), batch 1; physical-environmental-sciences is spent for this slot after six architectures, so the draw moves to education-learning-sciences (item-response-theory-test-equating, which serves ETL); new world, dataset, generator and shell
niche: an English heating-industry awarding body's heat pump installer theory paper, moved on 1 April 2026 from a centre-based paper scaled 0 to 100 to a new vendor's 60-question online paper scored by raw mark, conformed across both vendors' results and the candidate register so the Board can set the 2027 raw pass mark that holds the old standard of 65
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms both vendors' results through the candidate register, reads the Board's assessment policy correctly and holds the standard the way an awarding body holds it through a paper change, by giving the new paper's first-time candidates in April to September 2026 the pass rate the old paper gave first-time candidates in the same months of 2025, files a pass mark of 40; every field is read and every filed rule applied, and the pass mark is wrong because the 2026 cohort is not the 2025 cohort, the Boiler Upgrade Scheme's expansion having brought experienced gas engineers in through the standard route, which no column marks; the candidates who sat both papers file 41 when their two results are read side by side, because a second attempt gains about four scaled points on any paper, as the candidates who sat the old paper twice show.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the raw mark on the new paper equivalent to the old pass standard, an equating function the field estimates from a linking design, read here through the candidates measured on both instruments once the retest gain every second measurement carries is removed, a gain measured on candidates measured twice on the old instrument and matched on their first result; with a hospital's or a utility's nouns there is no instrument change, no pass standard and no retest gain, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: the old vendor's results export with absent and voided entries beside sat ones and scaled scores only
the new vendor's online-proctored sittings timestamped in UTC against a UK local-time calendar, late-evening sittings crossing a day and a month
two candidate numbering systems tied by the Board's register, with candidates who re-registered after a lapse under a second Board number
the old vendor's centre codes against the new vendor's test-site names
proctor-review holds on online sittings released as results later
dates day-month-year in one vendor's file and ISO in the other's
stakeholder_role: the awarding body's Head of Qualifications, who puts the 2027 pass mark to the Board

world.org_type: an industry awarding body for heating engineers

driver: An instrument's change is read through the members measured on both the old and the new instrument, but each member's second measurement carries a gain that comes from having been measured before, and the members measured on both are the ones who fell short the first time, so setting their two results side by side lays the gain on the instrument; the gain is measured on members measured twice on the old instrument, matched on their first result, and the members measured once on each instrument are no help when a new intake has changed who comes.
driver_concrete: Read each candidate who failed the old paper before 1 April 2026 and sat the new paper after it against the candidates who failed the old paper in 2021 to 2025 and sat it again, matched on their first scaled score: the old paper's own retest record says what pass rate those candidates would have had on a second old sitting, and the new paper's raw mark that gives the cross-switch candidates that pass rate is the pass mark that holds 65; the first-time candidates' pass rate carried from 2025 and the cross-switch candidates' two results read side by side both file a higher mark.
stump: The default path holds the old paper's 2025 first-time pass rate on the new paper's 2026 first-time candidates and files a higher pass mark than the standard holds; the step that lands it there is reading a change in the cohort as a change in the paper, when experienced gas engineers came in through the standard route in 2026, and the candidates who sat both papers carry a second-attempt gain that the candidates who sat the old paper twice measure.

differentiation.task450: task450 equated a district's new grade-5 form through anchor items both groups answered (a non-equivalent groups design with common items); this build has no common item, links the papers through the candidates who sat both, and removes the retest gain their second attempt carries, measured on candidates who sat the old paper twice.
differentiation.task488: task488 calibrated new adaptive items whose assignment followed the recorded level; this build sets one cut on a whole new paper, and the bias is the linking sample's retest gain and selection on a failed first attempt, not item assignment.
differentiation.task202: task202 cut a distribution of items whose record states only each unit's average, so the spread within units is lost; this build reads no distribution of averages and corrects a linking sample's retest gain, measured on members measured twice on the same instrument.
differentiation.task449: task449 read a record's characteristic through a link that for one class picks the first of several equally plausible targets; this build's link is exact (one candidate, two sittings) and the bias is what a second sitting adds, not which record is linked.
differentiation.task466: task466 fitted a yearly extreme to a recent full record and an older record that says only whether a threshold was passed; this build fits no extreme and no censored record, and sets an equating cut from a retest-gain correction.
differentiation.task196: task196 v1 rated experience where claim frequency repeats and severity does not; this build prices no risk, and its repeat is a candidate's second sitting whose gain is measured on same-paper retakes matched on the first result.
differentiation.task480: task480 v2 read a future increment from one cumulative total per unit whose yearly increment falls with age; this build reads no cumulative total and no ageing curve, and removes a retest gain from a linking sample to set one equating cut.
differentiation.task474 v6: Architecture 6 carried short traffic counts to a year by a facility's activity record (an unfiled carrying rule); this build files the estimand (the raw mark an equivalent group reaches at the old standard's pass rate) and leaves only the choice of the equivalent group open, which the old paper's own retest record settles.

lineage.architecture: v6 (a port authority's 2027 air-corridor designations from link-level on-road NOx, the terminal access roads' trucks carried to the year by the terminals' gate records)
lineage.driver: A period total at most sites follows the calendar pattern measured at always-on reference sites, but at the few sites that serve a single facility it follows that facility's own activity, which swings with an external schedule the reference sites never see; the facility's transaction record measures the swing, so those sites' two-day samples are expanded by the facility's activity on the sample days against its year, while expanding them by the reference calendar carries a busy or quiet week into the year.
lineage.stump: The default path expands every link's two-weekday count class by class with the classifying stations' factors and designates L01, L03, L05 and L06; the terminal access roads' combination trucks follow their terminals' vessel calls, which no station sees, so only carrying those roads' trucks to the year by each terminal's daily gate record designates L03, L05 and L14.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-31 at the repair: the determinism judge returned SEND_BACK; no shipped text said how a two-weekday count becomes a year's vehicle-miles, the golden's carrying rule (follow the vessel calls through the terminal's gate record) was filed nowhere, so the standard classifying-station factoring filed another designation, and the fleet answers needed an unfiled VIN rule

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that shares a utility with the unit's control device, so when the utility fails the instrument goes dark while the control is off; the dark hours are filled at the uncontrolled level the instrument reads in its first hours back, times the hour's metered input, rather than from the unit's measured hours in the same operating state or from the hours either side, which the controlled hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills every unmonitored hour from the unit's own measured hours in the same start state and load, and designates AF-2, CB-1, DF-1, DF-3 and SR-1; the gaps that came with the plants' instrument air trips are hours when the SCR's air-operated ammonia valves had closed as well, which the first measured hour after each trip shows at about twenty times the controlled rate, so filling those hours at that uncontrolled level adds CB-2 and AF-1.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-20: reader 12 landed the call after the register's air-to-open grounding (1 of 6 readers since it went in; 11 of 12 overall missed); the asks' revision device held at 0 of 18 for both round-6 readers

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that is out mostly in the hours after the unit starts, when the quantity runs several times its steady level at the same operating point, so the missing hours are filled by the hour's start state, read from an every-hour operating log, rather than by a fit on the operating point that the steady hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills each unmonitored hour from the unit's NOx-on-load regression and designates the units that run steadily high, because the analyzers drop out mostly right after a start, when the cold catalyst lets NOx run at several times the steady rate; filling the missing hours by hours since start designates the hard-cycling units the program should fund.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-20: a round-2 reader landed the call with the start-state fill and kept every ask (score_reader exit 1)

lineage.driver: A total published only for coarse units in some periods is split across a crossing partition by each fine unit's value that period, estimated by scaling an every-period indicator, whose ratio to the target differs by unit, to the unit's own multi-period average of the target; the multi-period average alone carries moves from later periods into earlier ones and the indicator alone carries its own ratio.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-20 at stage 4: reader 1 landed the call by benchmarking SNAP to the survey level; reader 2 kept 27 of 27 ask figures
